subject: On-prem inference fabric — reference diagrams and staging blueprint
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nagy <sarah.nagy@acme-corp.com>; Acme Security <security-admin@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem inference fabric — reference diagrams and staging blueprint

Hi Sarah / Acme security team,

Thanks again for the sync earlier. As discussed, I'm sending the initial reference artifacts for the on-prem inference fabric we propose for your pilot cluster. The goal here is a lightweight, auditable topology that isolates model serving traffic, minimizes egress, and gives your ops team a clear staging cutover path.

Attachments included: inference-fabric-blueprint.pdf (diagram set), staging-runbook.md (step-by-step), acme-network-constraints.xlsx (your inputs converted to checklist).

High-level notes:
- Control plane (admin, metrics, config) sits in a management VLAN with restricted SSH and mTLS to the control nodes.
- Data plane (inference workers) run in tenant performance VLANs; KV cache & model weights are pinned to local/NAS storage to avoid cross-tenant cloud egress.
- Egress policy: allow only proxying through the egress appliance for model updates; telemetry uses buffered uploads to your S3-compatible ingest endpoint during maintenance windows.

Open items for this draft:
1) NAT/break-glass strategy for emergency outbound access (we sketched two options in the runbook).
2) Certificate rotation cadence with your KMS team (see page 4 of the blueprint).
3) Resource reservations for burst inference (we'll propose node sizing after you confirm peak P95 tokens).

Can we target Tue 2026-05-18 10:00am PT for a handoff call with your infra and security teams? I added Rishi and Kimberly from our infra/ops side — they will lead staging and acceptance.

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Customer Solutions – Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Nagy <sarah.nagy@acme-corp.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <security-admin@acme-corp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem inference fabric — reference diagrams and staging blueprint

Tessa — thanks for the artifacts, they look thorough. A few quick clarifying questions from our side after a first pass:

1) For the control plane VLAN, are you expecting a routed path from our management network or a dedicated L2 segment you will ship? Our compliance team prefers minimal routing between management and tenant networks.
2) The blueprint mentions "buffered telemetry uploads" — can you confirm encryption at rest during buffering and whether we can force uploads only during the maintenance window?
3) Regarding model updates, can we pin updates to a signed bundle and prevent outbound calls except to your update mirror (we have an allowlist requirement).

We can do Tue 10am PT but can you make it 11am PT instead? Our lead infra has a conflict at 10.

Also adding Acme Security on this thread for certificate cadence and KMS integration comments.

Best,
Sarah

--
Sarah Nagy
Senior Platform Engineer
Acme Corp

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nagy <sarah.nagy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security-admin@acme-corp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem inference fabric — reference diagrams and staging blueprint

Thanks Sarah — answers inline below and notes on what we'll update in V2 of the blueprint: 

1) Control plane connectivity: we recommend a routed path with strict ACLs (no default route) from your management VLAN to the control-plane VLAN. The reason is operational simplicity for certificate provisioning and monitoring. If your compliance team requires full L2 isolation, we can provide a hardened OOB bundle and a dedicated management appliance — we'll note both options in V2.

2) Telemetry buffering: yes — buffered telemetry is encrypted at rest using per-tenant keys (AES-256) managed by your KMS. Uploads can be scheduled and forced only within allowed maintenance windows; the runbook includes the cron examples.

3) Model updates: we fully support signed bundles and allowlist-only egress to our update mirror. We'll include the signed bundle verification steps in the staging-runbook.md.

New meeting time: Tue 2026-05-18 11:00am PT works for our team. I'll share a calendar invite.

Action items I captured:
- Redwood: update blueprint v2 with L2 alternative, add signed-bundle verification steps, and document break-glass NAT option (Rishi to pick preferred pattern).
- Acme: confirm maintenance window and provide peak token P95 estimate for node sizing.

I'll upload a revised PDF by Monday.

Tessa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sarah Nagy <sarah.nagy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Acme Security <security-admin@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem inference fabric — reference diagrams and staging blueprint

Quick ops notes ahead of the handoff call:

- KV cache egress: recommend a local sticky cache per tenant with a fallback to a read-only shared cache in a separate VLAN. That allows quick cold-start recovery without additional outbound.
- Break-glass NAT: prefer an internally-controlled NAT gateway with event-driven ACLs (via your ticketing system) rather than manual firewall rule changes. This maps cleanly to audit logs and our rollout automation.
- Node sizing: for the P95 throughput you shared (approx 250 concurrent inference sessions, 256 token avg), propose 8x A100 equivalents or 12x for bursty traffic. We'll produce a sizing table in the updated runbook.

Attachments: short checklist snippet included in the staging-runbook.md (we'll push the full doc after edits).

Rishi

Thanks Tessa / Rishi — all sounds good. We confirmed the maintenance window (Sundays 02:00–04:00 PT) and will provide the P95 estimate by EOD Wednesday. 11am PT on Tue works for our infra & security leads; they will join the call.

- Networking will confirm whether we can allow a routed ACL path; if not, we'll flag L2 isolation and prioritize the OOB appliance option.
